# Supported Features

The emulator implements **203 of 266** endpoints in the WorkOS OpenAPI spec (`@workos/openapi-spec@0.133.0`) (**76.3%**).

Endpoint coverage says whether a route exists, not whether a
feature is usable; for example, Directory Sync implements every endpoint the spec defines for it and is
still unusable, because nothing can create a directory. The **Set up** column is the one that
answers "can I actually emulate this?".

| Column     | Meaning                                                                     |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Read**   | `GET` endpoints implemented / defined in the spec                           |
| **Write**  | `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` endpoints implemented / defined in the spec   |
| **Set up** | How data gets in: ✅ seed file, ⚠️ API calls only, ❌ no way to create data |

✅ full · ⚠️ partial · ❌ none · — not applicable

| Organizations            | ✅ 6/6   | ✅ 10/10 | ✅ seed `organizations`        | IT contacts are stored lowercased, capped at 20 per organization, and listed whole under null cursors, as production does. An organization is held to one active Admin Portal invitation — inviting any contact while one is active conflicts, the holder included — but nothing is emailed: the setup link an invitation would send is recorded on the contact and served by no route. Revoking clears the organization's invitation through any contact, since no route reports which one holds it. The `403` and `503` these routes document are not implemented — the store is not environment-scoped, so the forbidden case cannot arise — but both can be injected through the error hooks. Domains are stored lowercased and validated as production does: a `domain_data` entry needs a `state` of `pending` or `verified`, and a malformed domain, a domain listed twice or a public consumer domain (production's list, vendored) is `422` before the organization is written; the organization's own duplicate on `POST /organization_domains` is `409 domain_already_exists`, but two organizations may share a domain, since production enforces uniqueness only behind a flag. `POST /organization_domains/{id}/verify` starts DNS verification — `201`, `pending`, the `dns` strategy and a fresh token; `400 domain_already_verified` once verified — and resolves no DNS, so a domain gets verified only by seeding `state: verified` or sending `domain_data[].state: verified`, which on update recreates the domain under a new id as production does. `external_id` is unique across organizations: `400 external_id_already_used` on create and update. |
| User Management          | ⚠️ 8/11  | ⚠️ 7/13  | ✅ seed `users`                | Email-change confirm/send and waitlist endpoints are not implemented. Passwords sent to create, update and the password-reset confirm are held to production's policy (10+ characters, 72 bytes at most, not containing the email, zxcvbn score 3+) and refused with production's error bodies; the breached-password lookup is not performed, and seeded passwords are written as given. A password reset token lasts 15 minutes, and confirming it signs the user out everywhere and verifies the email. A taken `external_id` is refused, and `email_verified` can be set but not unset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Authentication           | ⚠️ 3/4   | ⚠️ 4/5   | ⚠️ API only                    | All grant types are hand-written rather than generated from the spec, and only production's public grant names are accepted: anything else is the 422 production's body validation gives. Refresh tokens rotate on every exchange, with the documented 30-second replay grace period, and a refresh can only switch into an organization the user is an active member of. A pending_authentication_token is bound to the step that issued it, so an MFA challenge or email-verification gate cannot be skipped by spending its token on another grant.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Organization Memberships | ✅ 3/3   | ✅ 5/5   | ✅ seed `memberships`          | Seeded via `memberships` nested under an organization. A role slug must name a role of the organization or of the environment (`member` and `admin` always resolve, as production creates both with every environment), else `422 invalid_role`; listing wants an `organization_id` or `user_id`. Multiple roles are assumed enabled for the environment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Groups                   | ✅ 3/3   | ✅ 5/5   | ✅ seed `groups`               | Seeded via `groups` nested under an organization. Members reference a seeded membership by email. Names are unique within an organization (a bare `409`, as production renders it), `name` is at most 256 characters, `description` a non-empty string of at most 150, and a group holds at most 500 members.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Invitations              | ✅ 3/3   | ✅ 4/4   | ✅ seed `invitations`          | State is derived when an invitation is read, so one expires on its own: 7 days by default, or `expires_in_days` from 1 to 30. A second open invitation for the address, an existing account on an environment invitation, an unknown role slug, and accepting, revoking or resending a non-pending invitation are refused with production's codes. There is no DELETE route, as there is none in the spec.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| SSO                      | ⚠️ 5/8   | ⚠️ 4/11  | ✅ seed `connections`          | Seeded connections carry `profiles`, which drive the SSO login flow. `POST /connections` follows production: one SSO connection per organization (`connection_already_exists_for_organization`, with `organization_id` in the body), SAML and OIDC types only with their `saml_options` / `oidc_options` present, no `domains` field (seed-only), and a created connection starts `validating` until the first login through it activates it and emits `connection.activated`. `GET /connections` lists SSO connections only. `GET /sso/authorize` requires `client_id`, sends a `validating` connection through and redirects an `inactive` one back with `error=connection_unlinked`; `POST /sso/token` requires `client_id` and `client_secret` (an environment API key); authorization codes live five minutes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Directory Sync           | ✅ 6/6   | ⚠️ 1/2   | ✅ seed `directories`          | Read-only over HTTP, as production is: a directory is connected in the dashboard, so there is no POST route to emulate. Seed `directories` to get one, with its groups, its users, and group-to-role mappings resolved onto the organization membership (which then reports `directory_managed`); seeding emits `dsync.activated` (for a `linked` directory), `dsync.group.created`, `dsync.user.created`, and `dsync.group.user_added` for each seeded membership (queryable at `GET /events`, not delivered — seeded endpoints register after), and `DELETE /directories/:id` emits a delivered `dsync.deleted` — except for an `unlinked` directory with no groups, which production deletes silently. Removing a user from a group emits `dsync.group.user_removed`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Multi-Factor Auth        | ✅ 2/2   | ✅ 5/5   | ⚠️ API only                    | TOTP codes are accepted without verifying the shared secret.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| FGA / Authorization      | ✅ 19/19 | ⚠️ 24/26 | ✅ seed `roles`, `permissions` | Checks and effective-permission listings include direct and native group role assignments, live group membership, and ancestor inheritance (`parent_resource_id`). Group grants support create/list/get and removal by ID or criteria; bulk replacement is not implemented. Role, permission, and resource bodies follow production's slug patterns (`org-` prefix or a generated slug for organization roles), lengths, and whitelists, answering 422 with production's field messages. Environment roles cannot be deleted over HTTP, as in production; an organization role a membership still holds answers 409 `role_has_assignments`. The organization role priority endpoint takes `role_priority_order`, naming every applying role once; the emulator keeps one priority per role, so an environment role reordered through one organization is reordered everywhere. Resource types are not modeled: any well-formed `resource_type_slug` is accepted on roles and permissions, and permission scopes are not checked against the role scope. Every organization owns an implicit `organization` resource whose `external_id` is the organization `external_id`, falling back to the organization id; resources created without parent fields attach to it, and it cannot be created, updated, or deleted directly.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

| Webhooks                 | ✅ 1/1   | ✅ 3/3   | ✅ seed `webhookEndpoints`     | `POST` and `PATCH /webhook_endpoints` validate as production does: an HTTPS `endpoint_url`, a non-empty `events` list from the subscribable catalog, `status` of `enabled` or `disabled`, and a generated signing secret (returned on every read). One emulator-only relaxation: a plain `http://` URL is accepted for a loopback host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`), so a local receiver can be registered over the API. Seed an endpoint to point it at any other `http://` receiver, pin its `secret`, or subscribe it to every event with an empty `events` list. Delivery is fire-and-forget with a 5s timeout and no retries. Endpoints registered in a seed file do not receive events from that same seed file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## How this file is generated

Every column except **Notes** is derived, so the table cannot drift from the code:

- **Read** / **Write** come from cross-referencing the spec's paths against the routes
  registered in `src/workos/routes/`.
- **Set up** comes from the `EmulatorSeedConfig` keys in `src/index.ts`. A feature declaring
  a seed key that the interface does not define fails the build.
- **Feature** groups the spec's API-shaped tags into products, in
  `scripts/gen-supported-lib.ts`. A spec tag with no feature also fails the build, so a new
  WorkOS product cannot silently disappear from this table.
